domain_definition: All occupations involved in promoting, maintaining, or restoring health through direct patient care, technical support, administration, research, public health, and allied health professions.

occupations.title: Clinical Pharmacist (Hospital Inpatient)
occupations.domain_fit: Directly involved in medication therapy management, drug–drug interaction management, and prescribing decisions in acute care.
occupations.operational_pressure: High time pressure, high consequence of error, conflicting stakeholder demands
core_tasks: Review medication orders for appropriateness, interactions, and dosing.
Participate in interdisciplinary rounds to optimize pharmacotherapy.
Manage drug–drug interaction alerts and resolve discrepancies.
Provide medication counseling to patients and staff.
Monitor therapeutic drug levels and adjust dosing regimens.
decision_points: Whether to override or act on a drug–drug interaction alert.
Selecting alternative therapy when first-line options are contraindicated.
Determining dose adjustments for renal/hepatic impairment.
Prioritizing which medication reconciliation discrepancies to resolve first.

primary_scenario.trigger: Pharmacist notices discrepancy between medication reconciliation record and urgent prescription while prescribing physician is unavailable during night shift.
primary_scenario.decision: Whether to hold, modify, or dispense the medication.
primary_scenario.counterfactual_change: If prescriber had been available, decision would have been clarified immediately.

alternative_scenarios: During interdisciplinary rounds, pharmacist must recommend alternative antibiotic for septic patient with multiple allergies and renal impairment while team is under time pressure.
Pharmacist receives high-severity drug–drug interaction alert for patient on 15+ medications and must decide whether to override, modify, or escalate.

occupations.title: Registered Nurse (Intensive Care Unit)
occupations.domain_fit: Frontline monitoring, anomaly detection, and emergency response in high-reliability critical care.
occupations.operational_pressure: High time pressure, interruption-heavy, high consequence of error
core_tasks: Continuous monitoring of vital signs, hemodynamics, and ventilator settings.
Detecting early signs of deterioration (sepsis, arrhythmias, respiratory failure).
Administering medications and titrating infusions per protocol.
Coordinating with multidisciplinary team during emergencies.
Documenting patient status and communicating changes.
decision_points: Recognizing subtle signs of deterioration before overt crisis.
Deciding when to escalate to physician vs. manage independently.
Prioritizing interventions during simultaneous patient needs.
Interpreting conflicting monitor alarms and clinical signs.

primary_scenario.trigger: ICU nurse notices subtle changes in post-operative patient's respiratory pattern and oxygen saturation trend while managing two other unstable patients and receiving frequent interruptions.
primary_scenario.decision: Whether to escalate to physician, continue monitoring, or adjust interventions.
primary_scenario.counterfactual_change: If nurse had not been managing multiple patients, escalation would have occurred sooner.

alternative_scenarios: During code blue, nurse must prioritize medication administration, defibrillation timing, and communication while team leader is inexperienced.
Nurse detects discrepancy between ventilator alarm and patient's clinical appearance, requiring troubleshooting before calling respiratory therapy.

occupations.title: Radiologic Technologist (MRI/CT Specialist)
occupations.domain_fit: Technical imaging decisions with safety and diagnostic quality implications.
occupations.operational_pressure: Moderate time pressure, safety-critical, regulatory compliance
core_tasks: Positioning patients and selecting imaging protocols.
Adjusting technical parameters for image quality and safety.
Screening for contraindications (metallic implants, contrast allergies).
Troubleshooting equipment malfunctions.
Ensuring radiation safety and dose optimization.
decision_points: Whether to proceed with scan given patient safety concerns.
Selecting protocol modifications for complex cases.
Deciding when to repeat scans vs. accept suboptimal images.
Escalating equipment issues vs. continuing with workarounds.

primary_scenario.trigger: CT technologist screens patient with unclear history of metallic implants and must decide whether to proceed with time-sensitive scan while radiologist is unavailable.
primary_scenario.decision: Whether to proceed, modify, or delay scan.
primary_scenario.counterfactual_change: If radiologist had been available, decision would have been clarified immediately.

alternative_scenarios: During complex MRI, technologist must adjust protocol parameters mid-scan due to patient movement while balancing image quality and scan time.
Technologist notices inconsistent radiation dose readings and must decide whether to halt scanner, troubleshoot, or continue with modified protocols.

occupations.title: Medical Laboratory Scientist (Clinical Chemistry)
occupations.domain_fit: Diagnostic testing decisions with direct impact on patient diagnosis and treatment.
occupations.operational_pressure: Moderate time pressure, high consequence of error, regulatory compliance
core_tasks: Running and validating clinical chemistry assays.
Detecting and troubleshooting anomalous results.
Determining when to repeat tests vs. report results.
Interpreting quality control data and flagging out-of-range values.
Communicating critical results to clinicians.
decision_points: Whether to report an anomalous result or repeat the test.
Identifying instrument malfunction vs. true patient abnormality.
Deciding when to escalate to pathologist or supervisor.
Prioritizing which critical results to communicate first.

primary_scenario.trigger: Laboratory scientist detects critically abnormal potassium result that conflicts with patient's clinical picture and must decide whether to report, repeat, or escalate while stat turnaround time is expiring.
primary_scenario.decision: Whether to report, repeat, or escalate result.
primary_scenario.counterfactual_change: If patient's clinical picture had been available, decision would have been more informed.

alternative_scenarios: During high-volume shift, scientist must prioritize which critical results to communicate first while managing multiple instrument alerts.
Scientist notices trend of out-of-range quality control values and must decide whether to halt analyzer, troubleshoot, or continue with modified protocols.

occupations.title: Physical Therapist (Outpatient Orthopedics)
occupations.domain_fit: Clinical judgment in rehabilitation planning with patient-specific adaptations.
occupations.operational_pressure: Moderate time pressure, resource constraints, reputational pressure
core_tasks: Assessing patient movement patterns and functional limitations.
Designing individualized treatment plans.
Modifying exercises based on patient response.
Determining progression vs. regression of interventions.
Documenting outcomes for insurance authorization.
decision_points: Selecting initial treatment approach from multiple options.
Deciding when to progress, maintain, or regress interventions.
Determining when to refer back to physician vs. continue therapy.
Balancing patient preferences with evidence-based protocols.

primary_scenario.trigger: Outpatient PT must decide whether to progress post-surgical knee patient to weight-bearing exercises despite patient reporting increased pain, while insurance visit limits are approaching.
primary_scenario.decision: Whether to progress, maintain, or regress treatment.
primary_scenario.counterfactual_change: If insurance visit limits were not approaching, decision would have been less pressured.

alternative_scenarios: PT notices conflicting information between surgeon's protocol and patient's functional capacity and must decide which to prioritize.
During busy clinic day, PT must prioritize which patients to see first when two patients arrive late and one has acute pain.

occupations.title: Health Information Manager (Hospital)
occupations.domain_fit: Compliance, data governance, and resource allocation decisions with regulatory implications.
occupations.operational_pressure: Moderate time pressure, high regulatory exposure, conflicting stakeholder demands
core_tasks: Overseeing medical record completeness and accuracy.
Ensuring compliance with privacy regulations (HIPAA, GDPR).
Managing health information systems and data governance.
Responding to audit requests and regulatory inquiries.
Allocating resources for record management and coding staff.
decision_points: Determining whether to release medical records given incomplete authorization.
Prioritizing which compliance gaps to address first.
Deciding when to escalate potential privacy breaches.
Allocating staff resources between competing priorities.

primary_scenario.trigger: Health information manager receives urgent request for medical records from patient's attorney with incomplete authorization forms while hospital is under audit.
primary_scenario.decision: Whether to release, delay, or escalate request.
primary_scenario.counterfactual_change: If hospital were not under audit, decision would have been less pressured.

alternative_scenarios: During compliance audit, manager must prioritize which documentation gaps to address first while managing staff shortages.
Manager detects potential privacy breach in EHR system and must decide whether to halt access, investigate, or escalate immediately.
diversity_tags: Moderate time pressure high regulatory exposure

occupations.title: Clinical Research Coordinator
occupations.domain_fit: Compliance, planning, and resource allocation decisions in clinical research with regulatory implications.
occupations.operational_pressure: Moderate time pressure, high regulatory exposure, conflicting stakeholder demands
core_tasks: Recruiting and screening research participants.
Ensuring protocol compliance and regulatory documentation.
Managing adverse event reporting and safety monitoring.
Coordinating multi-site study logistics.
Preparing for audits and inspections.
decision_points: Determining participant eligibility when criteria are ambiguous.
Deciding whether to report an adverse event as related to study intervention.
Prioritizing which protocol deviations to address first.
Balancing recruitment goals with safety requirements.

primary_scenario.trigger: Research coordinator must decide whether to enroll participant with borderline eligibility criteria while study is behind on recruitment targets and IRB is reviewing similar cases.
primary_scenario.decision: Whether to enroll, delay, or escalate eligibility decision.
primary_scenario.counterfactual_change: If study were not behind on recruitment, decision would have been less pressured.

alternative_scenarios: During multi-site study, coordinator detects potential adverse event and must decide whether to report it as related to intervention while sponsor is pressuring for faster enrollment.
Coordinator preparing for audit must prioritize which protocol deviations to address first while managing staff shortages and competing study deadlines.
diversity_tags: Moderate time pressure high regulatory exposure

occupations.title: Public Health Epidemiologist
occupations.domain_fit: Forecasting, risk assessment, and planning decisions with population health implications.
occupations.operational_pressure: Moderate to high time pressure, high consequence of error, political/reputational pressure
core_tasks: Analyzing disease surveillance data and identifying outbreaks.
Designing and evaluating public health interventions.
Communicating risk to stakeholders and the public.
Coordinating multi-agency response efforts.
Preparing reports and policy recommendations.
decision_points: Determining whether a cluster of cases constitutes an outbreak.
Selecting intervention strategies from multiple options.
Deciding when to escalate to emergency response.
Balancing transparency with public panic in communications.
constraints: High consequence of error (public health impact)

primary_scenario.trigger: Epidemiologist detects unusual cluster of respiratory illness cases and must decide whether to declare outbreak while data is incomplete and media attention is increasing.
primary_scenario.decision: Whether to declare outbreak, continue monitoring, or escalate response.
primary_scenario.counterfactual_change: If data had been complete, decision would have been more informed.

alternative_scenarios: During multi-state outbreak, epidemiologist must prioritize which intervention strategies to recommend while resources are limited and stakeholders have conflicting preferences.
Epidemiologist must decide how to communicate risk to public when preliminary data suggests potential threat but confirmation is pending.
diversity_tags: Moderate to high time pressure political/reputational pressure

occupations.title: Respiratory Therapist (Hospital)
occupations.domain_fit: Emergency response, monitoring, and troubleshooting decisions in respiratory care.
occupations.operational_pressure: High time pressure, interruption-heavy, high consequence of error
core_tasks: Managing mechanical ventilation and oxygen therapy.
Responding to respiratory emergencies (codes, rapid responses).
Performing pulmonary function tests and interpreting results.
Educating patients on inhaler techniques and breathing exercises.
Troubleshooting ventilator and oxygen delivery equipment.
decision_points: Adjusting ventilator settings based on patient response.
Deciding when to escalate to physician vs. manage independently.
Prioritizing which patients to see first during high-demand periods.
Interpreting conflicting monitor data and clinical signs.

primary_scenario.trigger: Respiratory therapist notices deteriorating oxygen saturation trend in mechanically ventilated patient while managing multiple patients and receiving frequent interruptions.
primary_scenario.decision: Whether to adjust settings, escalate to physician, or continue monitoring.
primary_scenario.counterfactual_change: If therapist had not been managing multiple patients, escalation would have occurred sooner.

alternative_scenarios: During code blue, therapist must prioritize airway management, ventilator setup, and medication timing while team leader is inexperienced.
Therapist detects inconsistent ventilator alarms and must decide whether to troubleshoot, call for assistance, or escalate immediately.

occupations.title: Medical Coder (Inpatient)
occupations.domain_fit: Compliance, classification, and adjudication decisions with financial and regulatory implications.
occupations.operational_pressure: Moderate time pressure, high regulatory exposure, conflicting stakeholder demands
core_tasks: Reviewing medical records and assigning diagnosis/procedure codes.
Ensuring coding compliance with guidelines (ICD-10, CPT).
Querying clinicians for documentation clarification.
Responding to audit requests and denials.
Monitoring coding accuracy and productivity metrics.
decision_points: Selecting primary diagnosis when multiple conditions are present.
Determining whether documentation supports a higher-level code.
Deciding when to query clinicians vs. code from available information.
Prioritizing which records to code first during high-volume periods.

primary_scenario.trigger: Medical coder must decide whether to assign higher-level diagnosis code when documentation is ambiguous while hospital is under.
